classes.purpose: Client-side avatar/appearance controller for a player (and pet) character. It turns an appearance description (gender + equipment part ids + face/eye/weapon ids) into a live CryEngine skinned character: it creates/rebuilds the character instance, binds equipment part skin-attachments across ~8 slots, attaches eye_left/eye_right offsets, spawns master/slave weapon entities, and precaches all avatar-related assets. All 18 methods were auto-tagged 'GetManagers' by the RTTI-string heuristic; only the first is the manager singleton accessor, the rest are appearance/model logic.

methods.purpose: One-time-init accessor that registers/returns the StcMbrNameSvr<CInfoManager> singleton for CAvatarInfo records (guarded by DAT_123be984, returns DAT_123be968). This is the CInfoManager<CAvatarInfo> lookup table used by FUN_11679e10(&x,"CAvatarInfo",0) everywhere else. This is the only method that genuinely matches the 'GetManagers' name.

References special model id 0x530e8.

Applies an appearance-description struct (param_2) to a character instance (this+0x24): sets base model (atoi param_2+0x14 via FUN_10aebd60), applies gender/face part (param_2+0x44 via FUN_10aec690), iterates the equipment red-black-tree at param_2+0x4c binding each part model, binds base skin (param_2+0x2c), and applies the decal/tint vector at param_2+0x7c.

Diffs the new appearance data (param_2 tree) against current cached part ids (this+0x1fc+slot*4, slots 1..6), sets per-slot changed/hidden flags (this+0x221+slot), copies the pending attachment-string block (this+0x230.. -> this+0xdc, 8 x 0x24), recreates the character via ICharacterManager, and re-attaches eye_left/eye_right. Returns a 'changed' bool. Reads eye_left/eye_right bone names.

Reads the 6 equipment part ids from an appearance tree (param_2 map at +0x4c and atoi param_2+0x2c), looks up each CAvatarInfo record's model string (+0x2c), copies each into a local string vector and pushes the base name via FUN_1083ab70. Used to gather the model file list for one appearance.

Same collection as 10aecda0 but the source is an explicit int id array (param_1[1..param_2]): for each id, looks up the record and its model string (+0x2c), building a string vector. First arg param_3 is a name pushed via FUN_1083ab70.

Walks an appearance tree (param_3 at +0x4c) resolving ids via FUN_1052bc30, and for the base (+0x14), each tree entry (+0x28), face (+0x2c) and extra (+0x44) calls FUN_10ad9880 to bind attachments/particle effects to the character (param_1). local_8 carries a resolved context id (from +0x28 of the '1' entry).

Pet variant of ApplyAttachmentsAndEffects: same tree walk but resolves records against the CPetAvatarInfo manager (CPetAvatarInfo::GetManagers) and binds via FUN_10ad9c00. Handles base(+0x14), tree entries(+0x28), and extra(+0x44).

Full rebuild of the avatar character from the embedded avatar-data block (this+0x18c). Resolves the 8 decal/tint slots (data+0x354..0x369) via the CAvatarInfo manager, copies pending state (data+0x230->0xdc, data+0x1fc->..), destroys old attachment objects, creates a fresh ICharacter (ICharacterManager +0xc/+0x14), attaches eye_left/eye_right, applies base model (data+0x1fc), per-slot equipment models (data+0x200..0x214), and skin tint via FUN_10aebd60/FUN_10ad9400.

Incremental appearance update for the local player: compares 8 slot triples in param_2 (each {id,x,y} at +i*0xc) against cached (this+0x4d+i*3), tracks per-slot model-changed (local_34) and transform-changed (local_7c) flags, updates decal/tint streaming flags (this+0x224), re-binds eyes, and plays the customization anim 'Co_0001c_anim'. param_3 forces full detach of all 8 slots.

Global precache of every avatar-related asset. Iterates CFaceInfo manager records to stream male/female_skeleton_<faceId>.cdf, precaches weapon *_firemode.xml (CatWeapon/Jade/M015/GiantSword/Hammer/Dagger/GunWeapon/LongSword/Bow), pet skeleton + AI blackboard XMLs, UIInput.xml, novice weapon fxparams, PlayerFSM WE00..WE10 FSMStates.xml, and ambient character cdf (meat, fish pole, float, fish, bridge) plus fallback player body .chr files.

Builds appearance for a networked/other entity (param_2 = character). Reads gender (vtbl +0x2ec). Live path (editor flag DAT_1202e818+0x209==0): loads eye/face texture ids (FUN_11348ac0 indices 0xf7..0x110 and 0x144..0x159), then FUN_10c0a6a0/FUN_10ad9400/FUN_10c09510/FUN_10c09690 to build body+equipment+skin. Preview path: applies default outfit using fixed CEquipInfo ids ('20002'/'620002' male, base/'610002' female).

Creates the two weapon-holder entities '<name>_Master' and '<name>_Slave' as class 'BasicEntity' (spawn flags |0x480000) via the entity system, then applies weapon models: base weapon (param_2+0x14), per-tree weapon parts (+0x28), main weapon (+0x2c), and firemode/effect resources (record +0x6c/+0x94) via FUN_10c09510/FUN_10c09690/FUN_10c0aee0. Copies parent transform to both weapon entities.

Returns (param_1) a string vector of the model names for the 6 body/equipment parts (from param_2 tree/atoi) that actually resolve to an existing streamable resource — validated by the resource-exists checks (DAT_1202e818+0x58 vtbl+0xf4 then +100 vtbl+0x100). Used to compute the set of models needing load.

Applies an explicit equipment id list (param_2 = int vector) to the large player-info layout: maps each record to its slot (record+0x14, <8), compares vs cached this+0x899+slot, marks changed slots (this+0x2284+slot) and dirty flag (this+0x8ff). On dirty, rebuilds skin attachments (vtbl +0x1dc), and if param_3 clears/reloads the character (+0x4b0), resets slot cache and reattaches (FUN_10ad9400 with this+0x8a4).

Main 'apply full appearance from data tree' for the player-info layout. Reads 6 part ids (param_2 tree +0x4c / atoi +0x2c), diffs vs this+0x899, sets per-slot flags this+0x2284 and dirty this+0x8ff, rebuilds skinning (vtbl +0x1dc). Also reads gender (vtbl +0x2ec) and, per param_2 flags (+0x8d/+0x8e), toggles a movement/physics param (this+0x8e3, skeleton vtbl +0x134 with 0.1f) and updates a sub-controller (FUN_10f1dee0).

Collects the 6 resolved part model strings into caller vector (param_4) checking streamability (vtbl +0xf4), diffs vs this+0x2264 cache; if changed, queries the entity script table for 'Properties.fileModel' (via entity proxy vtbl +0x150/+0x38/+0x28) and stores it. Returns 1 when a fileModel was found. Used as the load gate in UpdateAsyncLoadState(10ae4120).

Master builder for a player entity from its script + avatar data. Reads gender and 'ChangeModel', swaps body model ('male_fileModel'/'female_fileModel'), gathers equipment models (live: from character; preview: fixed CEquipInfo ids), applies skin, then reads entity-script tables: Properties/PlayerProxy for MasterWeapon/SlaveWeapon/SyncWeapon, spawns '<name>_Master'/'<name>_Slave' BasicEntity weapons, and applies EyeAttachmentOffset (male/female) with Leye_offset/Reye_offset/Leye_rotation/Reye_rotation to the eye_left/eye_right attachments.

classes.notes: CAvatarInfo is the CLIENT-side rendering/appearance controller (CryGame.dll), not a pure TLV data record; the auto-tag 'GetManagers' on all 18 methods is a false RTTI-string match (the singleton-accessor string "CAvatarInfo::GetManagers" is reused as an allocator tag inside every method). Only 1052bb90 is a real manager accessor. IMPORTANT: two distinct object layouts appear under this class: (a) a compact avatar-data layout using cachedPartIds at +0x1fc and stream flags at +0x221 (used by 10ae4120/10aeadc0/10aeddc0 etc.), and (b) a larger player-info layout using +0x899 (word idx) part ids, +0x2284 flags and +0x8ff dirty flag (used by 10f01650/10f02190/10f02e50/1103bc00). Layout (a) is likely the object pointed to by (b)'s +0x18c field. The param_2 'appearance-description' struct (fields +0x10/+0x14/+0x2c/+0x44 strings and a std::map at +0x4c) is a parsed XML/entity-property description, NOT a TLV wire struct; it maps conceptually to TlvAvatarBriefInfo (sex/equips) but the offsets do not match the TLV field ids, so treat the TLV link as directional only. All field offsets are inferred from control flow (no DebugFormat/printer method exists in this bundle), hence medium confidence.

classes.purpose: Static item-definition (base item config) record loaded into a CInfoManager<CItemBaseInfo> singleton and looked up by item id. Holds an item's id, internal/config name, display name, type/subtype category, per-type stack/carry limit and various boolean gameplay flags. Almost none of the 41 grouped functions are true members of the class: the auto-grouper collected every function that references the manager-singleton name string "CItemBaseInfo::GetManagers". Most are consumers in OTHER classes (bag/inventory validators, resource precachers, crafting/equip/NPC-sale logic) that resolve the item table via the singleton and do a 2D-sparse-array GetById.

methods.purpose: The real accessor. Lazily registers the name "CItemBaseInfo" with StcMbrNameSvr<CInfoManager> (guarded by DAT_123bdbfc one-shot flag) and returns the CInfoManager<CItemBaseInfo>* stored at DAT_123bdba0. All other functions inline a copy of this to reach the item table.

Parses a chat/GM command struct (char* fields at +0x18/+0x28/+0x38/+0x48), matches the leading token against "gm" (compare vs 0x6d67), _strtoui64-parses numeric args, and drives the HornNumDialogOK/HornNumDialogCancel numeric-input dialog. Resolves an item via the manager. Low confidence on exact command semantics.

Calls CAvatarInfo::GetManagers, reads a character/avatar info struct (fields +0xb8..+0xe4, name strings +0x50/+0x68/+0x80) and pushes strings/arrays to a network/render sink via vtable+0x32c; copies equipment id vectors (+0x19c..+0x1ac). Aborts with puts("out of memory")/exit on alloc failure. Client appearance/equip snapshot builder; only incidentally touches the item table.

Iterates a collection (vtable+0x18 count, vtable+0x1c getAt), resolves each id in the item manager, strcpy_s copies the item display name (+0xb4) into a 32-byte buffer, and emits it via a UI/message sink (FUN_111e0a50 vtable+4, tag 0x32).

If param_1[5]==*param_2, walks an entry array (this[0xd]..this[0xe], stride 0x20), string-compares (FUN_100fd0c0) each entry name against param_2+2 and, when equal and entry[0x18]==param_2[1], sets entry[0x1c]=1 (a 'matched/selected' flag). Low confidence on owning class.

Looks up a CManufactureInfo record by id, reads result item (+0x58), fields +0x60/+0x64/+0x78/+0x7c and a materials vector (+0x84..+0x88, stride 0x20). Resolves item display names (+0xb4) and emits recipe header (tag 0x74) and per-material rows (tag 0x77) to a message sink. Medium confidence.

Reads a manager/table via param_1[3], builds two copied lists (0x38-byte records) with memcpy, resolves item names (+0xb4) into 0x40 buffers, and sends each record (tag 0x106). Uses a red-black-tree membership test on ids. out-of-memory guarded. Low confidence.

Copies param_2[0..5] into this[0x7bf..0x7c4]; if the item id (this[0x7c1]) resolves and item.type(+0x34)==4 and item[+0x11c]==2, stores item[+0x16c] into this[0x7bb]; then invokes vtable+0x1a4 with &this[0x7bf]. Applies an equipped item's derived bonus/id to an actor.

Given add/remove lists (two vectors, stride 0x18 and 0xc), accumulates per-item running counts in an RB-tree keyed by hash, then checks each item's stack/carry limit via FUN_113f9ee0 (item+0x48) against existing count. Returns TDR-style error codes 0x34 (bad id range), 0x40, 0x32, 0x29 (capacity), 0 on success.
Simplified sibling of 113fc2e0: builds count map keyed by FUN_11669730 hash over add/remove vectors, validates against item stack limit (+0x48). Returns 0x32, 0x28, 0.

Full inventory add/remove validation over two operation vectors (this+0x8/0xc and +0x14/0x18). Derives an item category (0/1/2/5/9 from item.type +0x34, flags +0x68/+0xc4), computes needed slots via FUN_113f7100, and enforces per-item stack limit (+0x48) and per-category grid capacity. On failure writes error code to param_2+0x50 (0x28 stack, 0x29 grid, 0x2a category, 0x35 empty) and offending id to param_2+0x58; returns bool.
Resolves a CNpcSaleInfo record by id, walks an item's price/component vector (item+0x9c..+0xa0, stride 0x20), and computes a sale price with ceil()/double math (FUN_114b66e0). Medium-low confidence.

Consumes a list node stream (param_3+0x20 intrusive list), uses rand (FUN_100ee450) scaled by _DAT_11de98f0 over a min/max range to pick a count, resolves the item, validates via FUN_113f7d00/FUN_11521920, and appends granted (itemId,count,quality) triples into param_4; writes counts to out params. formulas: CInfoManager::GetById(id): let base=mgr+0x30, count=mgr+0x24, divisor=mgr+0x28, array=mgr+0x20. Valid iff id!=-1, !(id==0 && base!=0), divisor!=0, and 0 <= (id-base) < count. Then entry = array[(id-base)/divisor][(id-base)%divisor] (2D sparse bucket table). Same struct viewed via FUN_11679e10 result uses word indices [0xc]=base,[9]=count,[10]=divisor,[8]=array; linear enumeration uses [5]/[6] begin/end pointers, count=([6]-[5])>>2.

Bag validation error codes (written to op-struct+0x50): 0x28=per-item stack limit exceeded (offending id at +0x58), 0x29=grid/slot capacity exceeded, 0x2a=category capacity, 0x32/0x34/0x40=id out of table range, 0x35=empty/invalid op.
Needed-slots for a stack add ~ ceil((requiredCount - existingCount) / perStackMax) i.e. (required - existing - 1 + perStack)/perStack (114014c0).
NPC sale price computed with double math + ceil() over an item price/component vector (114b5ed0).
Drop roll count = base + floor(rand01 * (max-min+1)) then item/limit validated (114bcea0).

classes.notes: The 41 grouped functions share only the singleton-name string "CItemBaseInfo::GetManagers"; only ~4 are genuine CItemBaseInfo members (the manager accessor 10254050 and its inlined duplicates 11a87b20/11a880c0, plus the table query FindItemsByName 1159dc20). All record field offsets are inferred from consumer usage (Ghidra had no param types); none came from a dedicated DebugFormat/TLV reader in this bundle, so offset confidence is medium. The dump function 1187f880 is the strongest evidence for name fields and manager layout.

NO XML/TLV reader (Read_0x99) is present in this bundle, so the CPetSkillInfo struct is loaded elsewhere; field offsets below are INFERRED from the serializer/printer builders (112f6b70, 112f73a0, 112f6dd0) and the debug-log selector (1158b730). Cross-ref: the short* list processed by 11584a50/11588cc0 (count at [0], entries stride 6 shorts, sub-block at short offset 0x3d = byte 61) matches TlvSkillSlotData (count int16 @0, slotCount sub-struct @offset 61) and TlvSkillGroupData (skillGroup/skillCnt/skillID[]). Treat the field table as medium-confidence.
formulas: CInfoManager sparse-id lookup (used everywhere): idx = id - base(mgr+0x30); valid if 0 <= idx < capacity(mgr+0x24); bucket = *(int*)(mgr+0x20 + (idx / bucketSize(mgr+0x28))*4); record = *(int*)(bucket + (idx % bucketSize)*4).
CInfoManager linear enumeration: count = (mgr+0x18 - mgr+0x14)>>2; record[i] = *(int*)(*(mgr+0x14) + i*4).

Weighted random skill pick (1158b730): total = sum over list of record[+0x50]; rand = frand() * _DAT_11de98f0 * (total-1); iterate list subtracting record[+0x50] from rand, pick the record at which the running value first goes < 1; result id written to *param_3.
Skill effect rate (113f0ca0 / 113f0ff0): FUN_113e5380(animId, 0, (float)(record[+0xb0] / DAT_11de99b8)) — +0xb0 is an integer rate divided by a constant to a float.

Passive/aura match filter (11589800 / 115899c0 / 11589b80): apply if (record[+0x44]==0x12 || record[+0x44]==target[+0x70]) && tier rule on record[+0x70] vs target[+0x6c] (both <3, or 2<record<=target) && record[+0x48] <= target[+0x48] && record[+0x4c]!=0 && !FUN_1174ca30(record[+0x10]).
Next-level existence (112f4fe0 / 115889c0): true if some other record has other[+0x24]==rec[+0x24] && other[+0x14]==rec[+0x14]+1 (same skill group id, level+1).
Per-category cap on equipped list (11584a50): entries grouped by record[+0x58]; local_30[category] counter incremented, gated by FUN_1174bf40(category, currentCount); records with +0x58 < 6 rejected.

classes.notes: All 29 functions were auto-labeled 'CBuffInfo::GetManagers' only because they reference the CInfoManager<CBuffInfo> singleton-name string; their real behavior varies widely (event building, serialization, effect spawning, cross-reference validation) and several almost certainly belong to combat/entity/message-handler classes rather than to CBuffInfo itself. CBuffInfo is the static buff DEFINITION class (managed by CInfoManager, keyed by buffId); TlvBuffInfo is the separate runtime instance struct - do not conflate them, and the TlvBuffInfo field offsets do NOT map to the definition-record offsets recovered here (0x420 category, 0x424 group, 0x80 effect, 0x110 script). No reader for the core CBuffInfo definition record appears in this batch; the only reader (11a39890) loads GodLuckType/addbuff/sQaSI into a different (likely reward/luck) config class and is flagged as probable mis-bundling. The paged-array manager lookup (offsets 0x20/0x24/0x28/0x30) and the hit-descriptor layout (6 damage floats, 10 buff-id slots at 0x25, 4 spAttack elems at 0x1a/0x1c/0x1e/0x20) are consistent across the event/serialize functions. Field offsets on the definition record are inferred from usage, not from a DebugFormat printer, so confidence is medium.

classes.purpose: Static config/registry class describing a game Level (a hub/expedition map instance) in Monster Hunter Online. It is managed by the global CInfoManager<CMHLevelInfo> singleton and aggregates the quests, spawn groups, item drops, hub-entry configs and league schedule attached to a level. Almost every method here is an accessor/iterator over that manager keyed by level id, or a collector that walks the level's sub-lists and validates their referenced Info records (CHubEntry*, CSpawnMonsterGroupInfo, CItemBaseInfo, CLeague*).
